newsitem.title: CANADA: IRAN, ALGERIA, INDONESIA KEY WHEAT MARKETS-CWB.
newsitem.headline: IRAN, ALGERIA, INDONESIA KEY WHEAT MARKETS-CWB.

text.p: Iran, Algeria and Indonesia may make up some of China's waning demand on the world wheat market in the 1997/98 (Aug/July) crop year, Canadian Wheat Board's chief commissioner told an industry briefing here.
"We think some of the markets you might want to watch in the coming year will certainly be Algeria, Iran is a market you might want to watch and Indonesia," CWB chief commissioner Lorne Hehn said.
Iran bought 2.027 million tonnes of western Canadian wheat in 1996/97 placing it ahead of China which bought 1.684 million tonnes in the same period, CWB figures show.
China produced a record 110 million tonne wheat crop in that time that cut into it's need to draw from the world market.

Chinese output is likely to set another record in the current crop year at 114 million tonnes while Iran's wheat output was expected to be unchanged this year at 10 to 11 million tonnes, Hehn told Reuters after the briefing.

"We expect we'll at least sell the equivalent of wheat we sold to Iran last year," Hehn said. "I think in all of the big markets we expect we'll have market share where it was last year, or more, that's our goal."

The CWB held a 19 percent share of the world milling wheat market in 1996/97, 66 percent of world durum wheat exports, 40 percent of the world malting barley market and a 17 percent share of the world's feed barley market, he said.

Indonesia was seen as a market likely to grow as the world's largest miller, Jakarta-based Bogasari Flour Mills, imported 4.0 million tonnes of wheat in 1996/97 and was expected to purchase 5.0 million tonnes by 2000/01, he said.
The CWB sold 1.2 million tonnes of wheat to Indonesia in 1996/97, he said. Algeria accounts for 40 percent of world durum purchases but is also a large milling wheat importer.
